Papilionidae.description: Large to very large, strong-flying butterflies including birdwings, roses, mimes, Mormons, jays, swordtails, and banded peacocks. Many species carry prominent hindwing tails and feed actively while fluttering their wings at flowers.
Papilionidae.traits: Three pairs of fully functional walking legs; large rounded or tailed hindwings; caterpillars carry an eversible forked osmeterium behind the head.
Papilionidae.photoTip: Both upperwing (dorsal) and underwing (ventral) photographs help separate mimics, mimes, and closely related dark Papilio species.

Pieridae.description: Medium-to-small butterflies dominated by white, yellow, orange, and black pigments, ranging from garden grass yellows and emigrants to hill-dwelling clouded yellows and forest albatrosses.
Pieridae.traits: Six functional walking legs; most species rest with wings closed vertically over the back and frequently mud-puddle in moist riverbeds.
Pieridae.photoTip: Capture the closed-wing underside when possible, spot counts in Eurema and wingbar markings in Appias and Ixias are key underside clues.

Nymphalidae.description: Tamil Nadu’s largest butterfly family (97 checklist species), encompassing tigers, crows, pansies, eggflies, sailers, barons, rajahs, browns, and Tamil Nadu’s state butterfly, the Tamil Yeoman.
Nymphalidae.traits: Forelegs are reduced into short brush-like structures, so adults perch using only four walking legs; wings vary from cryptic bark-like undersides to bold iridescent uppersides.
Nymphalidae.photoTip: Record both basking upperside and resting underside views, especially for bushbrowns, treebrowns, sailers, and oakleaf butterflies.

Riodinidae.description: Small, forest-edge shade-loving butterflies represented in Tamil Nadu by two Plum Judy species (Abisara echerius and Abisara bifasciata).
Riodinidae.traits: Quick, jerky flights among shaded bamboo and undergrowth, typically settling with wings half-open and turning abruptly after landing.
Riodinidae.photoTip: Approach slowly along shaded forest paths and photograph the forewing white bands and hindwing twin spots.

Lycaenidae.description: Small, jewel-like butterflies (96 checklist species) including grass blues, pierrots, lineblues, ceruleans, silverlines, oakblues, royals, flashes, and sunbeams.
Lycaenidae.traits: Often bright metallic blue, copper, or orange above with intricate spotted or banded undersides; many carry delicate hair-like hindwing tails and false-head eyespots.
Lycaenidae.photoTip: Sharp macro shots of the hindwing underside bands and spot alignments are usually far more diagnostic than upperside blue.

Hesperiidae.description: Compact, fast-darting butterflies (83 checklist species) such as awls, flats, angles, aces, bobs, demons, swifts, and grass darts.
Hesperiidae.traits: Stout moth-like thorax, widely separated antennae with hooked tips (apiculus), and rapid darting flight; many rest with wings tilted at two angles (jet-plane posture).
Hesperiidae.photoTip: Photograph both the upperwing hyaline spots and the underside hindwing spot arcs, essential for distinguishing swifts and aces.

Papilioninae.traits: Includes Graphium jays and swordtails, Pachliopta roses, Papilio swallowtails, and the Southern Birdwing (Troides minos).
Papilioninae.habitat: Forest edges, hill streams, gardens, scrub, and evergreen shola margins across Tamil Nadu.
Papilioninae.photoTip: Note hindwing tail shape, body colour (red vs black), and submarginal spot patterns.

Pierinae.traits: Includes Delias jezebels, Cepora gulls, Appias albatrosses/puffins, Colotis/Ixias orange-tips, Hebomoia, and Prioneris.
Pierinae.habitat: Spans dry scrub plains (Colotis), urban avenues (Delias), and wet evergreen hills (Appias, Prioneris).
Pierinae.photoTip: Capture forewing tip markings and underside hindwing vein patterns.

Coliadinae.traits: Yellow, pale green, or orange butterflies with rapid sustained flight and strong migratory behaviour in several species.
Coliadinae.habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural margins, scrub, riverbeds, and Nilgiri/Palani high-altitude meadows (Colias).
Coliadinae.photoTip: For Eurema grass yellows, zoom into the underside forewing cell to count the small dark cell spots.

Nemeobiinae.traits: Purplish-brown butterflies with pale forewing bands and twin black submarginal eyespots near the hindwing angle.
Nemeobiinae.habitat: Damp shaded forests, foothills, bamboo thickets, and wooded gardens.
Nemeobiinae.photoTip: Compare the angle and breadth of the pale median band across the forewing.

Libytheinae.traits: Unmistakable elongated labial palpi projecting forward like a beak; dark brown wings with orange-tawny patches.
Libytheinae.habitat: Hill streams, wet roadsides, forest clearings, and mud-puddling patches.
Libytheinae.photoTip: Inspect forewing orange band breaks and hindwing underside mottling.

Danainae.traits: Tough, unpalatable butterflies whose caterpillars feed on milkweeds and dogbanes; central to Tamil Nadu’s seasonal Eastern–Western Ghats migrations.
Danainae.habitat: Hills, plains, urban parks, and forest corridors throughout Tamil Nadu.
Danainae.photoTip: Count subapical spots and pale streaks in the forewing cell to separate Blue Tiger vs Dark Blue Tiger and the Crow species.

Charaxinae.traits: Stout-bodied, exceptionally fast-flying canopy butterflies often attracted to tree sap, rotting fruit, and damp sand.
Charaxinae.habitat: Deciduous and evergreen hill forests, foothills, and wooded estates.
Charaxinae.photoTip: Underside pale bands and tail length separate Common, Anomalous, and Blue Nawabs.

Satyrinae.traits: Shade-loving brown butterflies marked with concentric underside eyespots (ocelli) that frequently exhibit wet- and dry-season forms.
Satyrinae.habitat: Grasslands, forest understorey, bamboo groves, palm groves, and shaded gardens.
Satyrinae.photoTip: Underside ocelli sizes, brand marks, and discal line shape (straight vs curved) are crucial for species ID.

Heliconiinae.traits: Bright orange-tawny butterflies with dark spots, serrated margins, or pearlescent underside bands, including Tamil Nadu’s state butterfly, Tamil Yeoman.
Heliconiinae.habitat: Sunny clearings, grasslands, montane sholas, and forest paths.
Heliconiinae.photoTip: Compare hindwing underside bands and marginal scalloping to separate similar orange species.

Limenitidinae.traits: Gliding butterflies with characteristic black-and-white banded wings (Neptis, Athyma) or emerald-olive camouflaged upperwings (Euthalia, Dophla).
Limenitidinae.habitat: Forest trails, stream banks, orchards, and wooded gardens.
Limenitidinae.photoTip: Check whether the forewing cell streak is broken into spots or continuous, and compare underside ground colour.

Cyrestinae.traits: Delicate white wings patterned with fine dark contour-like lines and rusty-orange hindwing margins, represented by Common Map.
Cyrestinae.habitat: Hill streams, moist boulders, and wet evergreen forest paths.
Cyrestinae.photoTip: Capture open-wing dorsal views showing the fine dark map-like venation lines.

Biblidinae.traits: Warm brown or orange-black butterflies with wavy transverse bands and slightly scalloped wing margins.
Biblidinae.habitat: Open scrub, gardens, castor stands, and dry deciduous foothills.
Biblidinae.photoTip: Check wing margin contour (angled vs rounded) and hindwing sub-basal wavy lines.

Apaturinae.traits: Rapid-flying forest species with sexual dimorphism and mimicry (such as Painted Courtesan mimicking tigers).
Apaturinae.habitat: Mid- to high-elevation evergreen and moist deciduous hill forests.
Apaturinae.photoTip: Watch wet forest trails and mud patches where males descend briefly to puddle.

Nymphalinae.traits: Familiar, colourful butterflies featuring conspicuous eyespots, seasonal morphs, and dramatic dead-leaf underside camouflage.
Nymphalinae.habitat: Gardens, wetlands, agricultural bunds, scrublands, and hill forests.
Nymphalinae.photoTip: In Junonia pansies and Hypolimnas eggflies, both dorsal colour patches and ventral patterns aid rapid ID.

Curetinae.traits: Robust blues with brilliant silvery-white undersides contrasting against bright coppery-orange (males) or white (females) upperwings.
Curetinae.habitat: Moist forests, riverbanks, and shaded forest edges where males bask high on foliage.
Curetinae.photoTip: Look at the direction of the dark underside discal line to separate Indian, Angled, and Siva Sunbeams.

Miletinae.traits: Represented in Tamil Nadu by the Apefly (Spalgis epius), whose caterpillars feed on mealybugs rather than plants.
Miletinae.habitat: Gardens, orchards, scrub, and forest edges near scale-insect colonies.
Miletinae.photoTip: Underside pale grey wings crossed by numerous fine wavy brown striations distinguish the Apefly.

Polyommatinae.traits: Delicate small blues with distinctive underside spot chains, zebra stripes, or white-and-black pied markings.
Polyommatinae.habitat: Lawns, grasslands, damp sand, woodland edges, and hill paths across all elevations.
Polyommatinae.photoTip: Macro underside views showing hindwing sub-basal spots and tornal orange eyespots are essential.

Theclinae.traits: Often tailed hairstreaks with metallic silver bars (Cigaritis), deep violet-blue upperwings (Arhopala), or swift red-and-slate flashes (Rapala).
Theclinae.habitat: Scrub jungles, forest canopies, mistletoe-bearing trees, and rocky hilltops.
Theclinae.photoTip: Capture the hindwing tornal lobes, tail count, and arrangement of underside bands.

Coeliadinae.traits: Large, swift skippers active particularly at dawn, dusk, and shaded forest interiors; several possess metallic-green or bright orange markings.
Coeliadinae.habitat: Dense hill forests, bamboo patches, shaded ravines, and coastal scrub.
Coeliadinae.photoTip: Focus on the underside hindwing white/blue bands and dark tornal spots.

Pyrginae.traits: Skippers that commonly settle with wings spread flat against leaves or tucked underneath foliage.
Pyrginae.habitat: Forest trails, rocky streams, dry open grasslands, and hill clearings.
Pyrginae.photoTip: Dorsal open-wing photos clearly reveal white hyaline forewing and hindwing spots.

Hesperiinae.traits: Fast-flying tawny, brown, or black-and-yellow skippers that typically hold forewings and hindwings at different angles when basking.
Hesperiinae.habitat: Grasslands, paddy margins, palms, bamboo thickets, and forest undergrowth.
Hesperiinae.photoTip: Zoom into the underside hindwing spot pattern and forewing cell spots to distinguish swifts and darts.
